title: Daily Rhythm
concept: Two short moments a day, a morning hello and an evening catch-up, to keep you in touch with each other and not only the household calendar.
whenToUse: Every day, and the first thing to bring back when you feel like housemates, or every talk is logistics after a trip. Start with the evening catch-up only.
steps: Morning hello (5 minutes or less): ask how each of you feels about today. Phones down if you can.
Evening catch-up (about 10 minutes): talk about how the day actually went, and each name one thing you appreciated.
Keep the same times most days.
On a busy day, keep the minimum: a hello, an “I see you”, an appreciation, and a repair within 24 hours if anything stings.
Note yes or no for each of you for a week. If it’s slipping, move the time and keep both moments.

phrases.text: How are you feeling about today?

working: After dinner, before the laptops come out, A asks, “How did today actually go?” B talks about the meeting for six minutes. Nobody mentions the shopping list.
notWorking: In bed, B asks, “You good?” without looking up from the phone. That’s going through the motions, not catching up.
activity: Pick your exact times for the next 7 days and mark them where you both see them.
note: If it starts to feel like a checklist, call a Quick Sun Memory.
